svg.title: Restricted diagonal fibres and the actual quasicoherent product
svg.desc: The full embedding makes the restricted diagonal a base change of the affine full diagonal. Its coordinate algebra retains every coefficient path. The actual product algebra has its module adjunction and Ran image; a global exterior tensor equivalence and localization require further assertions. Exact projective-line and nonflat examples exhibit retained negative generators.
svg.text: The restricted diagonal retains the full derived path space
Complex projective connected curve; connected reductive H; all connective DG coefficients.
1. A full embedding gives a Cartesian diagonal square — RDI.1–RDI.3
Z(restricted)
Z(full de Rham)
Z(restricted) × Z(restricted)
Z(full de Rham) × Z(full de Rham)
full embedding
diagonal
affine diagonal
Cartesian
The fibre over (z,w) is their entire isomorphism space, including all higher paths.
2. The affine fibre has an actual DG coordinate algebra — RDI.4–RDI.8
Full framed Betti ambient: Y = Spec B; full stack [Y/H]; (y,h) maps to (y,h·y).
D = A ⊗ᴸ over (B ⊗ B) of (B ⊗ O(H)).
For unframed points, trivialize the two frame torsors and descend this algebra.
For every A → A′: D(z,w) ⊗ᴸ over A with A′ ≃ D(z over A′,w over A′).
All products and scalar extensions are derived; no flatness or lower bound is assumed.
3. The algebra lives on the actual product prestack — RDI.9–RDI.19
D(restricted) = diagonal pushforward of O(restricted).
QCoh(Z(restricted)) ≃ modules over D(restricted) in QCoh(Z(restricted)²).
Pullback is free module formation; pushforward forgets the action and preserves colimits.
The full module bar proves the two inverse maps, arbitrary base change and projection formula.
The Ran regular algebra maps to this same algebra under the canonical exterior functor.
A restricted exterior-tensor equivalence and localization remain additional statements.
4. A negative diagonal generator already changes components — RDI.21–RDI.26
Projective line, H = Gₘ, trivial system: D = C[t,t⁻¹,w], |w| = −2, d = 0.
At A = C[z], |z| = −2: components = C× × C z.
Positive even groups: C zʳ ⊕ C zʳ⁺¹ (r ≥ 1); odd groups vanish.
An elliptic curve adds two odd generators a,b, hence two odd homotopy families.
5. Nonflat reduction preserves a homotopy that truncation loses — RDI.27–RDI.30
A = C[ε]/ε²; K = A[a], |a| = −1, da = ε.
H⁰(K) = C; H⁻¹(K) = C εa; all other cohomology vanishes.
Full reduction: K ⊗ᴸ over A with C = Λ(a), in degrees 0 and −1.
Truncate first: H⁰(K) ⊗ᴸ over A with C has C in every nonpositive degree.
The old cycle εa reduces to zero; the new cycle a has no cycle lift to K.
Exact proof locators: §§3.151–3.157, RDI.1–RDI.30; Solutions3.CT,3.CU,3.CV.
Ran framework: AGKRRV, arXiv:2010.01906v2, “Identification of the diagonal”.
